title: [BUG] Slow forward for conv_dw and mlp in ConvNeXt
author: xiuqhou

comments.author: rwightman
comments.body:
@xiuqhou first of all, you can't time cuda forward like that, look up how

second, I have a benchmark script `benchmark.py` that can be used and the performance remains comparable from 2.1 to 2.9. Slightly improving over time.

I'd recommend torch.compile with these models, it helps with the awkward conv/norm permutes quite a bit.

I've fiddled with contiguous vs not in different places, it can help some case but then it'll hurt others so in the end I'm leaving as is without compelling evidence across a wide range of hardware and model sizes. torchcompile will eliminate the benefit of that in any case.

comments.author: rwightman
comments.body:
@xiuqhou 
Sorry pasted the wrong analysis in here earlier.. but I did run comparisons for this one. Using the benchmark.py script included in the root, ran two sets on PyTorch 2.9.1 vs 2.1.2 w/ and w/o torch.compile used. There is a 4090 in this machine. No suprises here. Inference throughput is similar but slightly better in the latest PyTorch, and there was a bigger improvement in 2.9.1 in the train throughput.
